summary: Changes how the overview estimates subscription spending for the selected date range (new calculatePaidCount based on the previous renewal date; the overview now loads all subscriptions, not just active ones), adds a cancelled_at date that is set when a subscription is switched off (new column, no migration), shows 'Cancel Date' and previous renewal date in the subscriptions table, and bumps a few packages.

statements.text: Nothing flagged (plain reads logins, payments, database changes and secrets. It doesn't run the code, and it can miss bugs.)
statements.why: The new cancelled_at column has no backfill: subscriptions switched off before this commit have no cancel date, and since pages/app/index.js drops ?active=true, calculatePaidCount (utils/date.js:365) counts them as paid again, overstating the overview's spend/balance figures. That's a money-figure problem tied to the database change; the caveat about missing bugs softens but doesn't cover it.

statements.text: • The app page now says "Estimated spent amount for selected date range.". /app
• The agent changed the subscriptions all and subscriptions update parts of your server in ways plain can't describe yet. Ask the agent what they do differently.
statements.why: True but uninformative: /all now returns every subscription (active filter and field whitelist removed) with prev_renewal_date and paid_count; /update now saves cancelled_at. Both still require login (withUserAuth) and are scoped to the user.

statements.text: • Subscriptions now also store the cancelled date.
• The agent also changed components/Card/Summary.js, components/Table/SubscriptionsTable.js, utils/dataExtraction.js and utils/date.js, in ways plain can't describe yet.
statements.why: All four really change behaviour (new estimate formula in utils/date.js, Cancel Date column and toggle setting cancelled_at in SubscriptionsTable.js, paid_count field rename in dataExtraction.js/Summary.js).

statements.text: 1. Update your database: run `npm run dbpush` (it runs `prisma db push`) on your computer and on your live database. The database's structure changed.
statements.why: package.json:15 'dbpush': 'npm run predev && prisma db push'; the project doesn't use Prisma Migrate, so db push is the correct way to add cancelled_at. Fixes the old misleading step.

statements.text: 7. Test anything that uses prisma: it was upgraded from ^4.10.0 to ^4.10.1.
8. Test anything that uses tailwindcss: it was upgraded from ^3.2.4 to ^3.2.6.

misses.what: The overview's estimated subscription spend (and total spent/balance) changes: the formula now counts payments from the previous renewal date, and subscriptions turned off before this change (no cancel date) are counted as paid again, inflating totals.

Switching a subscription off now records today's date as its cancel date (shown in a new 'Cancel Date' column); switching it back on clears it. The renewal date column now shows a date for inactive subscriptions too (used to show '-'), plus a 'prev:' date.
/api/subscriptions/all now returns all subscription columns (field whitelist removed), including internal ones like nameHash/user_id, but only for the logged-in user's own rows.
